explanation: A pendulum's period T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g) depends only on the rod length L and gravity g — not on the mass and (for small swings) not on the amplitude. Lengthen the rod and each swing slows down; gravity supplies the restoring pull that is largest when the bob is farthest from vertical. The red arrow is the tangential restoring force proportional to -g*sin(theta), which drives the back-and-forth motion shown by the dashed arc.
bullets: Period T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g): only length and gravity matter, not the mass.
The restoring force along the swing is proportional to -g*sin(theta).
For small angles the motion is simple harmonic, with theta = theta0*cos(omega*t).
